answer: Among the 289 NLS-Y79 respondents who were jailed at least once during 1985–1994 (ever_jailed == 1), median 1985 composite wealth was $720 — less than a quarter of the full-sample median ($3,400) and lower than the median for every race × sex cell of the full sample. Stratifying the ever-jailed subset by race and sex reproduces the well-known wealth stratification of the full cohort, but compressed into a small, jail-exposed population. Cell medians (race / sex / n / median 1985 composite wealth) are: white/female (12) ≈ $4,100; white/male (57) ≈ $2,000; hipanic/female (9) ≈ $0; hipanic/male (52) ≈ $700; black/female (16) ≈ $0; black/male (143) ≈ $800. Pooling across sex within ever_jailed, white ever-jailed respondents have median 1985 wealth ≈ $2,200 versus ≈ $320 for Black ever-jailed respondents — a white-to-Black ratio of roughly 6.9×. Pooled Hispanic ever-jailed median is $0, so the white-to-Hispanic ratio is undefined (denominator zero). Within-race gender patterns are heterogeneous and unstable: among white ever-jailed, women (n=12) have a higher median than men (n=57), roughly 2.05× (≈ $4,100 vs $2,000); among Black ever-jailed and Hispanic ever-jailed, the female-cell median is $0 with n=16 and n=9 respectively, so a male/female ratio is undefined. Comparing each ever-jailed cell's median to the corresponding full-sample race × sex median shows the ever-jailed subset is poorer than its full-cell counterpart in every cell, with the largest absolute gaps for Hispanic/male (−$3,710 vs $4,410 in the full sample) and white/male (−$3,400 vs $5,400). The descriptive pattern consistent with these data is therefore a stacked disparity: (i) jail exposure itself is associated with substantially lower 1985 wealth across every demographic cell (ever-jailed medians are below full medians everywhere); (ii) within the ever-jailed subset, white respondents carry a large wealth advantage over Black respondents (≈ 6.9× pooled) and over Hispanic respondents (whose pooled median is $0); and (iii) gender does not act uniformly — among white ever-jailed, women retain a higher median than men, while in the minority-race cells the female medians are $0. Three caveats are essential. First, three of the six cells are very small — black/female n=16, hipanic/female n=9, white/female n=12 (all <20) — so the medians for those cells, particularly the female zeros, are unstable and should not be over-interpreted. Second, the 'hipanic' category is the literal label in the supplied file (sic). Third and most important, composite_wealth_1985 is measured in 1985, but ever_jailed==1 is defined by any jail spell during 1985–1994; the jail exposure that defines the subset therefore post-dates the wealth measurement for everyone whose first 1985–94 spell occurred after 1985, so these are descriptive associations between jail exposure and prior (1985) wealth, not causal estimates of incarceration's effect on wealth.

payload.hypothesis: Among the 289 NLS-Y79 respondents with any 1985–1994 jail spell, median 1985 composite wealth is $720 and is stratified by race × sex: white/female ≈ $4,100 (n=12), white/male ≈ $2,000 (n=57), hipanic/female ≈ $0 (n=9), hipanic/male ≈ $700 (n=52), black/female ≈ $0 (n=16), black/male ≈ $800 (n=143). Within ever_jailed, pooled white-to-Black median ratio ≈ 6.9× ($2,200 vs $320) and the pooled white-to-Hispanic ratio is undefined (hipanic pooled median = $0). The ever-jailed median is below the corresponding full-sample cell median in every race × sex cell. Findings are descriptive associations, not causal effects, because 1985 wealth precedes most of the 1985–94 jail spells that define ever_jailed; three cells have n < 20 (9, 12, 16) and their medians are unstable.
payload.workflow: 1. Loaded data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013 rows × 6 cols; 0 NA). 2. Filtered to ever_jailed == 1 (n = 289), as defined in datasets.json for 1985–1994 jail spells. 3. Grouped by race × sex and computed cell count (n) and median composite_wealth_1985; also computed the overall median within the ever-jailed subset ($720). 4. Computed the same grouping on the full sample as context and the cell-level gap (delta_vs_full). 5. Computed disparity ratios: white vs Black pooled within ever_jailed (2,200 / 320 ≈ 6.88), white vs Hispanic pooled (undefined; hipanic median = $0), and male vs female within each race within ever_jailed (white: 2,000/4,100 ≈ 0.49; black and hipanic: undefined because the female median = $0). 6. No inferential tests, no recoding of the literal 'hipanic' label, negative wealth values retained, no survey weighting. Artifacts saved under artifacts/: analysis_ever_jailed_wealth.py (executed script), cell_medians_ever_jailed.csv (cell table + full-sample medians), disparity_ratios.csv (ratios), overall_ever_jailed.csv (overall median row), summary.md (concise narrative).
